content: This systematic overview of systematic reviews (SOSR) identifies multiple effective interventions that can be implemented as part of school health services (SHS) provided by healthcare professionals. However, it is challenging to draw a comprehensive conclusion regarding the overall effectiveness of SHS in improving the health of school-aged children and adolescents. This difficulty arises due to the heterogeneity of the systematic reviews included and the significant gaps in the existing literature. More than half of the systematic reviews analyzed focused on mental health and oral health interventions. However, no systematic reviews were identified that evaluated other critical health areas, such as vaccinations, communicable diseases, and injuries. Additionally, no systematic reviews assessed comprehensive SHS programs. To enable policymakers and school health leaders to make evidence-based recommendations regarding which services should be available in schools, who should deliver them, and how they should be delivered, further systematic reviews are necessary. These reviews should evaluate routine, comprehensive SHS and identify the characteristics that contribute to their effectiveness. Special attention should be given to the content, quality, intensity, delivery methods, and cost of these services. The World Health Organization (WHO) guideline on school health services emphasizes the need for systematic reviews to address these gaps. The methodology and findings of such reviews are critical for advancing the evidence base for SHS.
